papers.title: Arithmetical Foundations - Recursion. Evaluation. Consistency
papers.abstract: We fix constructive foundations for Arithmetic on a map theoretical, algorithmic level. In contrast to elementhood and quantification based traditional foundations such as Principia Mathematica PM, Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF, or v. Neumann-Goedel-Bernays set theory NGB, our fundamental primitive recursive theory PR has as its basic "undefined" (not further defined) terms just terms for objects and maps. Goodstein's axiomatic uniqueness rules are derived as theorems in PR - with equality definability as a side result -, S is obtained by predicate comprehension, and the equivalence of the theory of partially defined maps and the categorical theory of mu-recursion identifies mu-recursive maps and while-loops with partially defined maps. Keywords: Goedel theorems, primitive recursion, categorical free-variables Arithmetic, mu-recursion, totality

papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.abstract: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. However, its boolean formulation cannot natively represent quantitative criteria such as cost, confidence, or implementation choice. In practice, these considerations are introduced through ad-hoc scalarization or by augmenting the resource space, which obscures system structure and increases computational complexity. Therefore, we develop a quantale-enriched theory of co-design in which resources and functionalities are quantale-enriched categories and design problems are quantale-enriched profunctors, which lifts co-design from boolean feasibility to quantitative evaluation. Series, parallel, and feedback composition remain valid over any commutative quantale, and change-of-base maps between quantales yield heterogeneous composition, so that subsystems evaluated in different local semantics can be composed in a common framework. Numerical examples on a target-tracking system and a UAV delivery problem demonstrate this framework and show how it avoids the drawbacks of boolean-only formulations.

papers.title: Flat and very flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves on ind-schemes
papers.abstract: This is a paper about homological algebra of flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves. We recall and collect various techniques such as accessibility and deconstructibility, and adopt them to ind-schemes under various assumptions. We also discuss the foundations of the notion of an ind-scheme.

papers.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
papers.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

papers.title: Representability of Galois extensions
papers.abstract: We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$. This generalizes the \'etale fundamental groupoid of commutative rings and Mathew's weak Galois groupoid.

papers.title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms
papers.abstract: To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue. In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure. To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications. We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al. Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.

papers.title: Maximality of the Do\v{s}en--Petri\'c Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
papers.abstract: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapsto\chi_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$.

papers.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.

papers.title: The dual of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is an infinitary variety of algebras
papers.abstract: A metric compact Hausdorff space is a Lawvere metric space equipped with a compatible compact Hausdorff topology (which does not need to be the induced topology). These spaces maintain many important features of compact metric spaces, but the resulting category is much better behaved. We prove that the category of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is dually equivalent to a variety of infinitary algebras.

papers.title: Relative involutions and inverses in monoidal dualities and slice constructions
papers.abstract: Our goal in this paper is to work towards developing a framework for characterizing dualities of weak categorical structures. It is often the case that duality involutions are characterized by relations which are more general than $f^2=1$. Moreover, it is also true that many dualities cannot be expressed using involutions alone. We develop a framework of relative involutions and relative inverses to express these dualities at least within categorical and bicategorical structures. In particular, we utilize this framework to express the dualities of virtual double categories and some important constructions on them. In the second part, we explore the problem of slicing and consider how dualities of monoidal structures interact with slice constructions. We end by providing a construction for both enriched slice model categories and enriched coslice model categories.

papers.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
papers.abstract: It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward. We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree. More precisely, for the pullback of a Lie groupoid along a surjective submersion, we construct an explicit cochain-level homotopy inverse to the natural pullback map. We first treat \v{C}ech groupoids, where the construction only involves a partition of unity, and then extend it to arbitrary surjective submersions, for which the extra choice of local sections is needed. We also show that the resulting operators preserve the complexes associated with $\mathcal{VB}$-groupoids, including homogeneous and $\mathcal{VB}$-cochains. As an application, we obtain explicit transfer maps for deformation cocycles of Morita equivalent Lie groupoids and recover the Morita invariance of deformation cohomology.

papers.title: Toward an Admissibility Theory of Aharonov--Bohm Arbitrage
papers.abstract: This note develops a provisional admissibility framework for Aharonov-Bohm type arbitrage. Starting from a categorical filtration $F:\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathsf{Prob}$ and its distortion on microscopic histories, we ask when a favorable closed microscopic loop can be realized as an executable relative ordinal arbitrage over an open macro-time interval. The history endofunctor $\mathsf{Hist}$ retains the staged decomposition of economic activities, while the twisted-arrow category $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ represents a microscopic loop as an arrow between distinct histories. An observable clock $\Pi: \mathsf{Econ} \to \mathcal T_{\mathrm{mac}}$ and a microscopic realization functor $J: \mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mac}}) \to \operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ connect economic histories with their microscopic geometry. Executability is treated separately through configuration histories, capacity constraints, observations, and policies. This yields pathwise and almost-sure notions of execution. A finite foreign-exchange model illustrates stochastic execution, capacity failure, terminal settlement, and comparison with a benchmark strategy. A parameterized finite filtration is constructed whose nontrivial statewise distortion agrees exactly with the relative FX settlement multiplier. Hence the resulting filtration--policy model satisfies the bridge $V_*(\pi^q)=dF(\gamma)V_*(\pi^p),$ and, under order compatibility, realizes relative ordinal arbitrage. The remaining problem is to identify the filtration parameters from independent market primitives and to study stability under refinement.

papers.title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $\xi \in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$.

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(\Lambda^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-mod})\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_{\lambda})\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, which are non-graded counterparts of the Koszul dualities of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

papers.title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions of Topological Invariants of Learned Representations
papers.abstract: When a learned representation is reused for a new task, which of its structure should survive? A task is a small category, a change of task is a functor $J$, and the invariants of a trained representation form a functor $F$. The left Kan extension $\operatorname{Lan}_JF$ is the invariant that the source and the change of task force on the target: by its universal property, every comparison of the source with an observed target invariant factors through it. The transfer discrepancy is the largest distance, over the target objects, between this extension and the observed invariant. For persistent homology the extension is a cokernel over comma categories, and a functorial version of the discrepancy, which also compares the maps between target objects, is $1$-Lipschitz under interleavings. On finite samples the discrepancy is a bottleneck distance, computed without approximation. For data glued from two pieces whose exclusive parts lie farther apart than the filtration scale, a Mayer-Vietoris sequence identifies what extending homology loses, while extending chains loses nothing. For a merge of labelled point clouds, the degree-zero discrepancy vanishes if and only if some $1$-Lipschitz classifier has a margin above the filtration scale at every sample point. In experiments on sampled manifolds, trained encoders and pretrained image models, every exact prediction holds on every sample. The discrepancy of truncated invariants recovers a hidden merge of separated parts far above chance and tells the intended target of a merge from a permuted control, but across pretrained models it does not track the accuracy of a linear probe.

papers.title: Distributivity, affineness, and the structure sheaf
papers.abstract: We observe that for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme the structure sheaf generates the perfect complexes if and only if the lattice of thick subcategories is distributive if and only if the affinization map is 0-affine. Examples are discussed, including an example of a quasi-projective scheme which is not quasi-affine but for which these equivalent conditions hold.

papers.title: On the internal homotopy theory of the motivic homotopy category
papers.abstract: We develop an $\infty$-categorical framework for internal homotopy theory (truncations, homotopy groups, and Eilenberg-MacLane objects) of an accessible localization of an $\infty$-topos. For the motivic localization over a perfect field $k$, we show that a motivic space has trivial motivic $n$-truncation iff it has trivial Nisnevich $n$-truncation ($n\geq-2$), identifying internal $n$-Eilenberg-MacLane objects with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of groups when $n=1$ and strictly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of abelian groups when $n\geq2$. We further prove that a generically free Nisnevich group sheaf is strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff it is birational (which for the free group sheaf $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ holds iff $A$ is birational), whereas for an \'etale-weakly unramified sheaf of sets $A$, $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ is $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff $A$ is itself $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Non-birational, \'etale-weakly unramified motivic sheaves of sets (such as $\mathbb{G}_m$) thus generate (non-abelian) $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves that are not strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Combining this obstruction with essentially smooth base change, we prove that for a qcqs scheme $S$, $\mathcal{H}^{mot}(S)$ is an $\infty$-topos iff $S=\emptyset$. We also study relative truncation and connectivity under a localization. Over a qcqs scheme $S$, this identifies external $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings with internal motivic $n$-coverings via pullback along the localization unit, yielding a motivic $n$-Galois correspondence over $k$. For connective morphisms over $k$, we establish a higher $\mathbb{A}^1$-Van Kampen theorem and a Nisnevich-local-to-global $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-connectivity criterion; in particular, a $k$-scheme is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected iff it admits a Nisnevich cover by $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected schemes whose pairwise fiber products have $k$-points.

papers.title: The geometry of Coherent topoi and Ultrastructures
papers.abstract: We show that coherent topoi are right Kan injective with respect to flat embeddings of topoi. We recover the ultrastructure on their category of points as a consequence of this result. We speculate on possible notions of ultracategory in various arenas of formal model theory.

papers.title: Cartesian Gray-Monoidal Double Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we present cartesian structure for symmetric Gray-monoidal double categories. To do this we first introduce locally cubical Gray categories, which are three-dimensional categorical structures analogous to classical, locally globular, Gray categories. The motivating example comprises double categories themselves, together with their functors, transformations, and modifications. A one-object locally cubical Gray category is a Gray-monoidal double category. Braiding, syllepsis, and symmetry for these is introduced in a manner analogous to that for 2-categories. Adding cartesian structure requires the introduction of doubly-lax functors of double categories to manage the order of copies. The resulting theory is algebraically rather complex, largely due to the bureaucracy of linearizing higher-dimensional boundary constraints. Fortunately, it has a relatively simple and compelling representation in the graphical calculus of surface diagrams, which we present.

papers.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
papers.abstract: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

papers.title: Categorical Diffusion of Weighted Lattices
papers.abstract: Quantales are well known in logic and computer science, and categories enriched in them unify ordered, metric, relational, and tropical structures. Problems in dynamic programming, synchronization, and discrete event systems require reconciling local data, represented by objects in a quantale-enriched category, across the edges of a network, represented by an undirected graph. Concurrently, replacing inner products with hom-objects and linear adjoints with adjoint functors initiates a categorification of graph and sheaf Laplacians, with a view toward enrichment in larger monoidal categories and bicategories. To this end, we lay the foundations for an enriched harmonic analysis on graphs through cellular sheaves of quantale-enriched categories and a Laplace operator that we call the Lawvere Laplacian. Over an arbitrary unital quantale, the weighted global sections of such a sheaf are the vertex data that agree across every edge up to the tolerances of a weight function. They form the quantale-enriched category of natural transformations from a weight diagram into the sheaf, which is a weighted limit when the quantale is commutative. When the restriction maps have right adjoints, we prove that the weighted global sections are the suffix points of the Lawvere Laplacian, which are the equilibria of its harmonic flow. Under a continuity hypothesis, the harmonic flow converges to the greatest weighted global section below its initial cochain, and for central weight functions the weighted global sections form a complete coreflective subcategory of the cochains. Instances of the theory include the Bellman--Ford iteration over the Lawvere quantale, the reconciliation of local cost estimates, quantale and clock synchronization, and coupled max-plus discrete event systems.

papers.title: Presheaves and cocompletions in formal category theory
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between presheaf constructions and free cocompletions in the context of formal category theory, elucidating the coincidence between the two concepts in familiar settings. We show that, in a virtual equipment satisfying mild assumptions, free cocompletions under classes of weights are exhibited by presheaf constructions. We furthermore extend the theory of weighted colimits from enriched category theory to this setting, developing the concepts of atomicity and rank, and providing recognition theorems for presheaf objects, free cocompletions, and cocomplete objects. As an application of our methods, we construct free cocompletions, under arbitrary classes of colimit-small weights, of (possibly large) categories enriched in (not necessarily symmetric) monoidal categories and bicategories; this resolves a longstanding omission in the literature on enriched category theory. As a consequence, we obtain a categorified Eilenberg--Watts theorem, which extends the classical theorem for categories of modules for rings (seen as one-object Ab-enriched categories) to categories enriched in a bicategory.

papers.title: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras via generalized hep-derivors
papers.abstract: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras are many-sorted algebras whose carriers are strict higher-order categories and whose operations are higher-order functors. They admit a homogeneous and a heterogeneous presentation, both by partial algebras whose operation domains are given by existence equations. To relate these presentations and their dimensions, we introduce generalized hep-derivors between hierarchical equationally partial signatures. A generalized hep-derivor selects carriers by existence equations in one variable and interprets operation symbols by terms, with operation domains evaluated recursively in the transformed algebra. Every generalized hep-derivor induces a functor between categories of many-sorted partial algebras. The values of this functor satisfy the domain conditions wherever their operations are defined, and we characterize when the operations are defined exactly where these conditions hold. The functor induced by a composite receives a natural inclusion from the composite of the induced functors; this inclusion, which can be strict, makes the induced functors a normal lax indexed category. In finite dimensions, generalized hep-derivors realize graduation and unification as an equivalence between the homogeneous and heterogeneous presentations, and discretization as a left adjoint to truncation. In dimension $\omega$, we reconstruct the categories of $\omega$-categorial algebras as projective limits of their finite-dimensional truncations and obtain unification by a quotient construction; we also establish algebraic squares and compatibility with change of signature. Finally, for nonempty sets of sorts, we show that the finite-dimension condition in the homogeneous $\omega$-presentation is not axiomatizable by quasi-existence equations on its fixed signature.
